sources.entry: OpenSign ⚠ - Document signing software (alternative to DocuSign). (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: OpenSign is a free, open source document e-signing application positioned as an alternative to DocuSign.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a web app for signing PDF documents with hand-drawn, uploaded, typed, or saved signatures and for annotating PDFs. It supports multiple signers, including sequential signing order and signing links, and email one-time-code verification for guest signers. Documents can be set to expire, signers can reject with a reason, and templates can be created for repeated use. It keeps audit trails and generates a completion certificate, and offers an API with API keys plus a Zapier integration. Deployment is described via Docker Compose using a HOST_URL environment setup, with a non-persistent default MongoDB that the user should replace for durable data.
use_cases: Collect electronic signatures on PDF contracts
Send documents to multiple signers in a set order
Track audit trails for signed agreements
Integrate e-signing into existing software via API
how_to_run: Make sure Docker and git are installed
Set HOST_URL and run the curl download command from the README (Linux/macOS), or the PowerShell/CMD equivalent on Windows
Follow the Installation Guide in the project docs for detailed setup
notable: Email OTP verification for guest signers
Sequential multi-signer workflow with expiring documents and signer rejection
Audit trail and completion certificate generation
Public API with API key generation and Zapier integration
caveats: Default MongoDB in the Docker deployment is not persistent and is cleared on restart unless you supply your own MongoDB URL
Awesome-selfhosted lists the project with a warning marker, and the README does not describe its maintenance status
Some features (such as OpenSign Drive and integrations) are described without detail about hosting requirements
